Dear Sir,
We are sorry to learn that you felt inconvenienced, and we sincerely regret any misunderstanding that may have occurred. Client satisfaction and professional integrity are of utmost importance to us, and we always endeavour to act transparently and strictly in accordance with law.
To place the correct facts on record, on the very day you approached our office, you were informed that I would be out of station for approximately two weeks due to prior professional commitments, as I was required to attend matters before the Hon’ble Delhi High Court and thereafter the Hon’ble Patna High Court. Despite this, your matter was taken up without delay, and the eviction notice was duly drafted and dispatched through the Post Office.
When the draft notice was provided to you, there was not a single point left out, nor was any mistake pointed out or correction suggested by you. The draft was approved by you in its entirety, reflecting the care and diligence with which the work was carried out. We work very hard to achieve results for our clients and always do our best in their interest.
The notice was posted at the true and correct address provided by you, which is clearly mentioned in the notice itself. After dispatch, and with bona fide intention, we supplied you with copies of the notice and postal receipts so that you could independently track the status from the official website of India Post, ensuring complete transparency and leaving no scope for doubt.
The postal article was returned with the endorsement “Intimation Posted”, which, as per settled legal principles, constitutes good and valid service in law. This is a matter of record, supported by the returned envelope bearing the endorsement of the postal authority. Therefore, this cannot be construed as a mistake and/or deficiency in service.
Upon receipt of the returned article, I personally called you and informed you about the status and requested you to visit the office so that the postal record, legal implications, and further remedies could be explained to you in detail. Unfortunately, instead of seeking clarification from us or visiting our office, conclusions were drawn at a very initial stage, and enquiries were made directly at the Post Office. Had you approached us for clarification, the position would have been clear and the misunderstanding could have been avoided.
On the first meeting in the morning, I could not give you sufficient time for a detailed discussion as I was required to urgently leave for court, which was clearly conveyed to you. This was not out of disregard but due to professional obligations. We are not greedy, and we always give preference and priority to our clients over monetary considerations. During our second meeting in the evening, I informed you that our morning hours are extremely hectic due to court work and that detailed discussions are best held later in the day.
We respectfully state that we are always answerable to our clients for every step taken. The records available speak for themselves. The present issue appears to have arisen due to misunderstanding rather than any negligence or unprofessional conduct.
That said, we genuinely apologise for any inconvenience you may have felt. I am a person who believes in learning and continuous improvement, and your feedback has helped me realise the importance of clearer follow-ups. I assure you that necessary precautions will be taken so that such situations do not arise again.
Even today, we remain ready and willing to assist you. We humbly request you to kindly visit our office for clarification and give us one opportunity to address your concerns, if any.

We felt saddened that before posting this review, no clarification or concern was shared with us, despite our availability.

Warm regards,
Mr. Nityanand Yadav
Principal Advocate
Shree Bhagwat Law Associates
